title: Eye-friendly theme with high-contrast text across all screens

requirements.summary: Update global CSS custom properties in index.css to use a softer, eye-friendly color palette with sufficient contrast ratios for accessibility
acceptanceCriteria: Background colors across all screens are warm but not stark white or harsh — a soft parchment/ivory tone that does not cause glare.
Body text and heading text colors are dark with at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against their background.
Deep teal accent color is softened/desaturated to reduce eye strain while remaining distinct.
Gold accent text meets minimum contrast when used as label or heading text.
No text appears invisible, near-invisible, or same-color-as-background on any screen.

file_operations.description: Update CSS custom properties for light mode to use softer, eye-friendly colors: replace current background/parchment tones with warmer lower-saturation values (e.g., #f7f3ec), soften dark teal accents to muted medium teal, ensure all foreground/text colors use dark values with 4.5:1+ contrast ratio against backgrounds (WCAG AA), and darken gold accent for text legibility. Retain the Unani/Islamic manuscript aesthetic while improving readability. Also update PWA theme_color and background_color in manifest.json to match the new palette.
Update theme_color and background_color fields to match the new eye-friendly palette defined in index.css, ensuring consistency across PWA presentation.

requirements.summary: Audit and fix text color declarations across all screen components to ensure high-contrast, clearly visible text on all backgrounds and states
acceptanceCriteria: All option labels in QuizScreen and ReviewScreen are legible on both selected/highlighted and unselected states.
Correct-answer highlights show dark bold text on the green/teal highlight background (not white-on-white).
Incorrect-answer highlights show clearly readable text on the red/rose highlight background.
Card headings and body copy on HomeScreen, HistoryScreen, and SubscriptionPlansScreen all render in high-contrast dark text.
Form labels, input placeholders, and help text in AdminPanelScreen are clearly legible.
Navigation links in AppHeader dropdown are fully visible against the menu background.
Timer and counter text in QuizScreen is readable at all timer states including the red warning state.

file_operations.description: Audit and fix all text color declarations to ensure high-contrast visibility: ensure question text, option labels, timer text, and counter text use dark foreground colors with sufficient contrast against their backgrounds. Fix any selected/highlighted states where text color matches or is too close to the background. Ensure timer warning state (red) maintains readable text.

Audit and fix text colors for answer review items: ensure option labels are legible on both selected/highlighted and unselected states, correct-answer highlights show dark bold text on green/teal backgrounds (not white-on-white), and incorrect-answer highlights show clearly readable text on red/rose backgrounds.

Audit and fix text colors for result display elements: ensure score percentage, performance tier text, stat numbers (correct/incorrect/skipped counts), time taken, and topic breakdown labels all use high-contrast dark text against their card/background surfaces.

Audit and fix text colors for form elements and question list: ensure form labels, input placeholders, help text, and existing question display text all use clearly legible high-contrast colors against their backgrounds.

Audit and fix text colors for topic/year browser sections: ensure section headings, question text within expandable items, and action button text all use high-contrast dark colors that remain visible against card and list backgrounds.

Audit and fix text colors for history summary and attempt list: ensure summary stat headings and numbers, attempt date/score/time text, and card body copy all render in high-contrast dark text against card backgrounds.

Audit and fix text colors across hero banner, stats section, and navigation cards: ensure hero heading/subheading, stat labels and numbers, card headings, and card descriptions all use high-contrast dark text against their respective backgrounds.

Audit and fix text colors for plan cards: ensure plan names, billing cycle labels, price text, feature list items, and action button text all use high-contrast colors that remain clearly visible against card backgrounds and any highlight states.

Audit and fix text colors for header and dropdown navigation: ensure app title, menu button icon, and all navigation links in the dropdown drawer are fully visible against the header background and dropdown menu background respectively.

requirements.summary: Update Tailwind color token definitions to align with the new eye-friendly palette and ensure utility classes produce accessible results
acceptanceCriteria: Tailwind color tokens for foreground, muted-foreground, and primary-foreground all produce dark readable text.
Background tokens (background, card, popover) produce soft, low-glare surfaces.
The updated tokens are reflected consistently across all screens without needing per-component overrides.
No Tailwind utility class produces invisible or near-invisible text on its paired background.

file_operations.description: Update Tailwind theme color token definitions (OKLCH values for primary, foreground, muted, accent, card, and related tokens) to align with the new eye-friendly palette: use lower-saturation medium-brightness values for background tokens and softer but sufficiently dark values for text tokens. Ensure consistency with the CSS custom properties updated in REQ-52 so utility classes like text-foreground, bg-card, text-primary, and text-muted-foreground produce accessible, high-contrast results across all screens.
